app.name: Zeebx
audio.hint: Only the PCM that games hand over as a buffer plays for now. A refused format is named in the terminal.
calibration.toast.setting: Show a notice in the game while it calibrates the Boomerang
calibration.toast.title: Calibrating the Boomerang…
controls.art_hint: Press a button to see it light up, or click a part to reassign it.
controls.assigning: Press a key or button…  (Esc cancels)
controls.axes.hint: Four axes, and the left stick feeds the first two. The D-pad does **not** write to them: on the console it is a button, and a game that only listens to the axis never sees it — for those there is the option above.
controls.boomerang.calibrate_hint: To calibrate, leave the controller still on a flat surface, buttons up, and click Calibrate. Games still run their own calibration on top of this one.
controls.boomerang.calibrate_refused: Calibration refused: the controller was not lying still with the buttons up.
controls.boomerang.no_device: No controller with a sensor: the Boomerang stays still, with only the mapped buttons
controls.boomerang.no_sensor: {nome} has no motion sensor the emulator can read: the Boomerang stays still, with only the buttons
controls.boomerang.sensor_denied: {nome}: no permission to read the motion sensor
controls.boomerang.sensor_waiting: {nome} connected, waiting for the motion sensor
controls.boomerang.unlock_done: Rule created. The sensor starts responding within a second.
controls.boomerang.unlock_failed: Could not create the rule ({erro}). Create {arquivo} with the line below and reconnect the controller:
controls.boomerang.unlock_hint: The system asks for the administrator password once, to create a rule that gives your user access to controllers' motion sensors. No need to reconnect the controller.
controls.boomerang.unlock_waiting: Waiting for the password in the system dialog…
controls.dpad_to_analog: D-pad also on the stick (games that only read the analog stick)
controls.dpad_to_analog.hint: Each direction writes the full course on the X and Y axes, and releasing returns the axis to center. Turn it on only for games that ignore the D-pad: a game that reads both channels steps twice per press. The buttons keep working.
controls.hint: The keyboard always works; a chosen gamepad works alongside it.
controls.kind.boomerang.hint: The Zeebo motion controller. Boomerang Sports games (Dodgeball, Tennis, Volleyball, Peteca), Crash Nitro Kart and Zeebo Extreme play by motion. Motion comes from the controller chosen below, if it has a sensor: Wii Remote, Pro Controller, DualShock 4, DualSense. Hold the Wii Remote sideways, like a wheel, with the D-pad on the left; the others in the normal grip. With no controller chosen, the first paired Wii Remote feeds the first Boomerang and the second one the second.
controls.kind.hint: The Zeebo has two USB ports and accepts a keyboard. Every game uses the gamepad; keyboard is for seeing the console enumerate one.
controls.kind.pad.hint: Z-Pad and Dragon have the same buttons and axes; only the grip changes. To the game the difference is the USB identifier the controller reports, and some Boomerang Sports games change their handling by it.
controls.no_devices: No gamepad found. Plug one in and scan again.
controls.players_note: A second player needs the emulator to feed two pads, which it does not do yet.
controls.port.off_hint: Empty port. Turn it on for the console to see a device here.
controls.shortcut.is_screenshot: {key} is the screenshot shortcut. Change the shortcut first, below.
controls.shortcut.reserved: {key} already belongs to the game window: Esc closes, P pauses, F11 toggles fullscreen.
controls.shortcut.taken: {key} is already {button} on port {port}. Clear that button first, or pick another key.
controls.shortcuts.hint: They work in the game window, keyboard only. Esc, P and F11 are fixed.
debug.clock: Instructions per second and game clock
debug.hint: Information about the run, drawn over the game. Meant for hunting problems.
debug.log.empty: Nothing to report: this game wrote no log and the emulator has no complaints about it.
debug.log.hint: Opens in its own window, with what the game wrote. Can be exported as .log.
debug.log.title: Run log
graphics.anisotropic.hint: Keeps textures seen at an angle sharp, like tracks, floors and walls. Cheap. Stays off when the card lacks support.
graphics.antialias.hint: Smooths jagged polygon edges. Works together with the internal resolution. Foliage and fences drawn with cut-out transparency are unchanged.
graphics.aspect.hint: Experimental. Renders 3D scenes wider, showing more to the sides instead of stretching; HUD and 2D stay 4:3 in the center. Expect visual issues: objects popping in at the edges, since the game skips what it thinks is off screen, and the image returning to 4:3 when 2D is drawn on top. Requires 3D on the graphics card.
graphics.fog.hint: The fog belongs to the game: on the console it usually hides what the draw distance could not reach, and here the scene arrives whole. Turn it off to see further. Works on both rasterizers and takes effect right away.
graphics.gpu_present: Put the frame on screen through the graphics card
graphics.gpu_present.hint: The frame goes up in the format it is already in, and the card does the scaling. It does not change how the game draws, only how the finished frame reaches the screen.
graphics.gpu_rasterizer: Fill the 3D on the graphics card
graphics.gpu_rasterizer.hint: The console's 3D is filled by the card instead of the CPU. Measured: Z-Wheel 35% less time in the emulator, Crash on the track 19%. The drawing is not identical to the software one — about 1% of pixels differ a little. Takes effect on the next game you start, and falls back to software when no card is reachable.
graphics.internal_resolution.hint: Renders the 3D larger on the graphics card and scales it to the window. The game still sees 640×480. It only shows when the frame on screen is fully 3D; screens with 2D drawn on top stay at the console resolution. High factors are heavy on the card.
graphics.scaling.integer.hint: Never blurs, but leaves borders when the window does not fit a whole multiple — on a 1080p screen, 640x480 only fits at 2x (1280x960).
graphics.speed_limit.hint: Off, the emulator runs as fast as it can and games play too fast.
graphics.window.hint: F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen at any time. The game window choice applies to the next game.
language.name: English
library.controls_hint: D-pad or arrows pick · Button 1 or Enter plays · HOME opens the Z-Wheel
library.no_folder: No ROM folder chosen yet. Pick one in Settings.
library.title: Library
nav.search.hint: Filters the library by name, ignoring accents. Ctrl+F searches, Esc clears, Enter plays the first result.
nav.unlock_sync.done: Date moved back one day — Zeeboids should allow syncing and exporting again.
nav.unlock_sync.hint: Zeeboids only syncs once a day, and the limit is its own. Moves the date back one day.
nav.z_wheel.hint: Opens the console home screen. Games picked there open right here.
nav.z_wheel.missing: No Z-Wheel found. Point to or detect the Z-Wheel in the settings.
play.close.title: Close the game?
play.state.overwrite.hint: Press again to overwrite this slot.
play.state.title: Save states
play.state.unavailable: This file could not be identified; save states are unavailable in this session.
saves.confirm: Delete the save for {name}? This cannot be undone.
saves.device.hint: The file system games share. Zeeboids keeps its characters here, and Zeebo F.C. reads them from here.
saves.title: Save manager
settings.discord.covers.hint: Discord only shows images registered in the application or published online. Export the images and upload the folder under Rich Presence → Art Assets (file names are already the keys), or publish the covers and enter the address with {chave} or {clsid} in place of the game. Empty uses the application's images.
settings.discord.on: Show what I'm playing on Discord (Rich Presence)
settings.language.hint: Extra languages can be added as JSON files in the lang folder, without rebuilding.
settings.library_view.hint: Grid shows every game at once. Slider shows one game at a time, like the Z-Wheel: the logo roller on top, the box in the middle and the description below. Logos, boxes and descriptions come from the Z-Wheel set below.
settings.roms_folder.hint: Where Zeebx looks for games. A folder holding one directory per title, or the .mod files themselves.
settings.screenshots_folder.hint: Where the screenshot shortcut saves, one folder per game. With 3D on the GPU the image comes out at the internal resolution; with a HUD on screen, a 2D game or the software rasterizer, it comes out at 640×480, the Zeebo's resolution.
settings.title: Settings
settings.z_wheel.found_no_art: Z-Wheel found, but without its box art collection.
settings.z_wheel.hint: The Z-Wheel package (.zip, .mod or its folder). It opens from the top bar button, leaves the game list, and lends the library its box art, official names and descriptions.
settings.z_wheel_eol.hint: As the ROM ships: the bottom wheel has only "Play" and "Help". Off, it goes back to the earlier one: "Play", zeebo, "Buy" and "Setup". Takes effect the next time the Z-Wheel opens.
settings.z_wheel_transitions: Z-Wheel transitions on every screen change
settings.z_wheel_transitions.hint: The ROM slides each screen only the first time, and the dump already marks the main ones as seen. On, screens always slide. Takes effect the next time the Z-Wheel opens.
update.title: New version available
welcome.controls: Before starting a game, set up your controller in Settings → Controls.
welcome.development: The emulator is still in development. Some games and features may have issues, such as crashes or graphics and sound glitches.
welcome.dont_show: Don't show again until the next version
welcome.title: Welcome to Zeebx
